{{Short description|Population-based health survey in Denmark}}
{{AI-generated|date=December 2025}}
[[File:Herlev_Hospital,_with_the_2022_construction_additions,_seen_from_Herlev_Ringvej_2023_(cropped).jpg|thumb|447x447px|[[Herlev Hospital]] (2023), where the population survey takes place and is headquartered.]]
The '''Copenhagen General Population Study''' ('''CGPS'''; {{Langx|da|Herlev/Østerbroundersøgelsen}}) is an ongoing Danish [[Longitudinal study|longitudinal]] [[cohort study]], that investigates the [[epidemiology]] of a wide range of [[Disease|diseases]], in particular [[cardiovascular disease]], [[respiratory disease]], [[cancer]], [[Infection|infections]] and other [[Multifactorial disease|multifactorial diseases]], in a representative sample of the [[Demographics of Denmark|Danish population]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |date=2024-05-07 |title=Østerbroundersøgelsen |url=https://lex.dk/%C3%98sterbrounders%C3%B8gelsen |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=Lex |language=da}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |editor-last=Marcuslund-Reuss |editor-first=Anders |title=Østerbroundersøgelsen |url=https://www.bispebjerghospital.dk/afdelinger-og-klinikker/oesterbroundersoegelsen/om-undersoegelsen/Sider/default.aspx |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=www.bispebjerghospital.dk}}</ref> Headquartered at the Department of [[Clinical chemistry|Clinical Biochemistry]] at [[Herlev Hospital]], it was established in 2003 with professor [[Børge Nordestgaard]] as [[principal investigator]], and it is the world's largest [[population study]] that follows the long-term health development of a healthy population over time, currently collecting data on over 170,000 enrolled [[Research participant|participants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-10 |title=Ny folkesygdom: 'Fedtlever' er ved at gøre sit indtog |url=https://videnskab.dk/krop-sundhed/ny-folkesygdom-fedtlever-er-ved-at-goere-sit-indtog/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=videnskab.dk |language=da-DK |quote=undersøgelsen [er] verdens største, der følger en rask befolknings helbredsudvikling over tid. |trans-quote=the study [is] the world's largest to follow the health development of a healthy population over time.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2023 |editor-last=Andersen |editor-first=Stine Linding |title=DSKB Nyt |url=https://dskb.dk/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/202303_DSKBnyt_web.pdf |journal=Medlemsblad for Dansk Selskab for Klinisk Biokemi |issue=3 |issn=1902-1526}}</ref>

Expanding upon the earlier and less extensive sister study, the '''Copenhagen''' '''City''' '''Heart Study''' (CCHS; {{Langx|da|Østerbroundersøgelsen}}), the population survey has been conducted in several phases since 1976, incipiently involving a representative [[Sampling (statistics)|sample]] of people in the [[Østerbro]] neighbourhood of [[Copenhagen]]. In 2003, the CGPS was established to expand the study to cover an increasingly large area in the [[Copenhagen metropolitan area]]. A second phase is currently in progress for the study, whereas a sixth is underway under the auspices of CCHS.<ref name=":12" /> All participants are recalled for follow-up examinations, and are followed in the [[Det Centrale Personregister|Danish Civil Registration System]] and [[Medical record|medical records]].{{Sfn|Laugesen|Mengel-From|Christensen|Olsen|2023|p=229-230}} The survey includes a comprehensive [[physical examination]], preceded by a [[questionnaire]] on lifestyle [[Risk factor|factors]]. The examination covers heart and [[Spirometry|lung function]], measurements of height, weight, [[blood pressure]], [[Ankle–brachial pressure index|ankle-brachial pressure index]], extensive [[Venipuncture|blood sample]] [[Blood test|analysis]] and other clinical examinations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Projects – RH-CT |url=https://rh-ct.org/projects/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Since 1976, the study and its precursor have produced over 1,330 [[Scientific literature|scientific articles]] in the [[Medical literature|medical press]], including significant research in [[Epidemiology|general]] and [[genetic epidemiology]]. Notable findings include the positive impact of regular [[physical activity]] on lifespan, the health benefits of moderate [[red wine]] consumption, and the role of [[Triglyceride|triglycerides]] and [[genetic predisposition]] in developing various diseases.<ref name=":02" /><ref name=":12" />

As of 2023, 27 [[Thesis|doctoral theses]] and 96 [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] dissertations have been based on the study's data, with around 20 PhD students and hundreds of other researchers currently working with the data.<ref name=":12" />

== History ==

=== Precursor ===
The Copenhagen General Population Study is an offshoot of the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS), known in Danish as ''Østerbroundersøgelsen''. The CCHS was launched in 1976 by Professor [[Anders Tybjærg Hansen]] and [[Cardiology|cardiologists]] Dr. {{ill|Peter Schnohr|da|Peter Schnohr}}, Dr. Gorm Jensen and [[statistician]] Jørgen Nyboe, and began as a large [[Cardiovascular disease|cardiovascular]]-focused study. 

The study was launched in response to a sharp [[Post-war|post]] [[World War II]] increase in mortality from [[Myocardial infarction|acute myocardial infarction]] (AMI) in Denmark, particularly in the [[Capital Region of Denmark|capital region]]. From the 1950s onwards, cardiovascular disease emerged as a leading [[cause of death]], yet knowledge about its causes and [[Risk factor|risk factors]] remained limited. Inspired by large-scale [[Epidemiology#Types of studies|epidemiological initiatives]] such as the [[Framingham Heart Study]] (US), the [[Seven Countries Study]] ([[Ancel Keys|Keys]]), and the [[Whitehall Study]] (UK), Danish Professor Tybjærg Hansen initiated the national cohort study. It incipiently received funding from the [[Danish Heart Foundation]] and support from [[Municipalities of Denmark|municipal]] health authorities.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Jensen |first=Gorm Boje |date=2024 |title=Hvad er der kommet ud af Østerbroundersøgelsen? |url=https://bibliotek.kk.dk/work/work-of:870971-tsart:139971116?type=artikel+%28online%29 |journal=Lægemagasinet: fagtidsskrift for praktiserende læger |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=16-19}}</ref>

Although designed with a large emphasis on [[cardiovascular disease]], specifically [[Coronary artery disease|coronary heart disease]], [[hypertension]] and [[stroke]], it quickly expanded to include a wide array of health conditions, such as [[Respiratory disease|pulmonary diseases]], [[heart failure]], [[arrhythmia]], [[dementia]], and various genetic and [[psychosocial]] factors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prescott |first=Eva |date=14 December 2016 |title=Københavns Byhjerteundersøgelse (CCHS) 'Østerbroundersøgelsen' |url=https://ichgcp.net/da/clinical-trials-registry/NCT02993172 |access-date=15 November 2024 |website=Good Clinical Practise - Network}}</ref> The initial study population of the Copenhagen City Heart Study consisted of a random sample of nearly 20,000 men and women, aged 20 to 93, selected from approximately 90,000 residents aged 20 and older in ten wards around [[Rigshospitalet]] in [[Copenhagen]], encompassing all of [[Østerbro]] and one-third of [[Nørrebro]], [[District|districts]] of [[Copenhagen Municipality]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Peter |first=Schnor |date=23 October 2000 |title=Østerbroundersøgelsen - snart 25 år |url=https://www.skivebibliotek.dk/work/work-of:870971-tsart:85825488 |journal=[[Ugeskrift for Læger]] |volume=162 |issue=43 |pages=5788–5789}}</ref>

=== Establishment of the study ===
The Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) was established on 26 November 2003 at Herlev Hospital under the leadership of Professor [[Børge Nordestgaard]]. Designed as an expansion of this precursor study, it broadened the scope to include a larger and more diverse cohort from the [[Copenhagen metropolitan area]]. Initially, the study recruited over 100,000 participants aged 20 to 100, who contributed through [[Questionnaire|questionnaires]], [[Sampling (medicine)|biological samples]], and [[Physical examination|physical examinations]]. In 2010, ethical approval enabled the integration of cardiac [[CT scan|CT imaging]], providing insights into cardiovascular [[Biomarker|biomarkers]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Çolak |first1=Yunus |last2=Afzal |first2=Shoaib |last3=Nordestgaard |first3=Børge G |last4=Vestbo |first4=Jørgen |last5=Lange |first5=Peter |date=April 4, 2017 |title=Prognosis of asymptomatic and symptomatic, undiagnosed COPD in the general population in Denmark: a prospective cohort study |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/s2213-2600(17)30119-4 |journal=The Lancet Respiratory Medicine |volume=5 |issue=5 |pages=426–434 |doi=10.1016/s2213-2600(17)30119-4 |pmid=28389225 |issn=2213-2600|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The cohort has since expanded to include over 170,000 enrolled participants.

A key feature of the CGPS and its predecessor studies is the integration with Denmark’s comprehensive [[Personal identification number (Denmark)|national registries]]. These registries provide detailed and updated information on participants, including hospital [[Medical diagnosis|discharge diagnoses]], cancer records, causes of death, [[Prescription drug|prescription]] use, and [[Demography|demographic]] data such as education and income. This infrastructure ensures nearly 100% [[Follow-up studies|follow-up]], eliminating a common source of bias in [[Longitudinal study|longitudinal studies]]. The registries also enable cost-effective management of large cohorts and allow disease-free participants to serve as controls for case-control studies.<ref>{{Cite web |editor-last=Amin Hassan |editor-first=Hassan |title=Herlev Østerbroundersøgelsen {{!}} About the Study |url=https://www.herlevhospital.dk/afdelinger-og-klinikker/klinisk-biokemisk-afdeling/forskning/Sider/Herlev-oesterbroundersoegelsen.aspx |access-date=2024-11-15 |website=www.herlevhospital.dk}}</ref>

== Scientific impact and findings ==

=== Scientific findings ===
Numerous highly cited [[Scientific literature|scientific articles]] have been published on the results of the studies, for example that 65–79 year olds who start [[Exercise|exercising]] about 4 hours a week will increase their lifespan by an average of 4 years.<ref name=":02" />

One highly publicized result showed that moderate [[red wine]] consumption was associated with a significantly reduced risk of [[myocardial infarction]] and lower [[all-cause mortality]]. The finding was cited by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Bill Clinton]] and featured on [[CBS]]’s ''[[CBS 60 Minutes|60 Minutes]]'', sparking global interest.<ref name=":0" />

Other findings from the studies include the clinical implication of elevated [[triglyceride]] levels for the development of [[cardiovascular disease]] and the importance of [[genetic predisposition]] for the development of cardiovascular disease, [[Respiratory disease|lung disease]] and [[cancer]], among others.<ref name=":02" />

For example, in cardiovascular health, its findings established that elevated nonfasting [[triglyceride]] levels correlate with a heightened risk of [[myocardial infarction]], [[Coronary artery disease|ischaemic heart disease]], and [[Mortality rate|mortality]] in both men and women.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mortensen |first1=Martin B. |last2=Afzal |first2=Shoaib |last3=Nordestgaard |first3=Børge G. |last4=Falk |first4=Erling |date=2015-09-21 |title=The high-density lipoprotein-adjusted SCORE model worsens SCORE-based risk classification in a contemporary population of 30 824 Europeans: the Copenhagen General Population Study |journal=European Heart Journal |language=en |volume=36 |issue=36 |pages=2446–2453 |doi=10.1093/eurheartj/ehv251 |issn=0195-668X |pmc=4576144 |pmid=26082084}}</ref> Additionally, the study revealed nuanced effects of [[Alcoholic beverage|alcohol consumption]] on [[blood pressure]], showing that different types of alcoholic beverages may influence blood pressure differently.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mortensen |first1=Martin B. |last2=Afzal |first2=Shoaib |last3=Nordestgaard |first3=Børge G. |last4=Falk |first4=Erling |date=2015-09-21 |title=The high-density lipoprotein-adjusted SCORE model worsens SCORE-based risk classification in a contemporary population of 30 824 Europeans: the Copenhagen General Population Study |journal=European Heart Journal |language=en |volume=36 |issue=36 |pages=2446–2453 |doi=10.1093/eurheartj/ehv251 |issn=0195-668X |pmc=4576144 |pmid=26082084}}</ref>

In the field of genetic research, CGPS researchers has employed [[Mendelian randomization]] to uncover the [[Causality|causal]] links between long-term [[Alcoholic beverage|alcohol consumption]] and [[Coronary artery disease|coronary heart disease]] risk factors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lawlor |first1=D. A. |last2=Nordestgaard |first2=B. G. |last3=Benn |first3=M. |last4=Zuccolo |first4=L. |last5=Tybjaerg-Hansen |first5=A. |last6=Davey Smith |first6=G. |date=2013-08-02 |title=Exploring causal associations between alcohol and coronary heart disease risk factors: findings from a Mendelian randomization study in the Copenhagen General Population Study |url=https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/eurheartj/eht081 |journal=European Heart Journal |language=en |volume=34 |issue=32 |pages=2519–2528 |doi=10.1093/eurheartj/eht081 |pmid=23492672 |issn=0195-668X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In respiratory health, CGPS provided pivotal data on early identification of [[chronic obstructive pulmonary disease]] (COPD), emphasizing the roles of age and smoking exposure in disease progression and associated risks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Çolak |first1=Yunus |last2=Afzal |first2=Shoaib |last3=Nordestgaard |first3=Børge G. |last4=Lange |first4=Peter |last5=Vestbo |first5=Jørgen |date=2020-10-28 |title=Challenges in defining early COPD in the general population: Findings from the Copenhagen General Population Study |url=https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/56/suppl64/1398 |journal=European Respiratory Journal |language=en |volume=56 |issue=suppl 64 |page=1398 |doi=10.1183/13993003.congress-2020.1398 |issn=0903-1936|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The study's findings in [[Metabolism|metabolic]] health revealed that increased [[Lipid metabolism|triglyceride metabolism]], characterized by elevated levels of [[Plasma cell|plasma]] [[glycerol]] and [[Β-Hydroxybutyric acid|β-hydroxybutyrate]], is strongly linked to higher risks of [[all-cause mortality]], including deaths from cardiovascular diseases and cancer. These discoveries underscore the CGPS's broad impact on understanding the interplay of lifestyle, genetics, and metabolic factors in health outcomes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Johansen |first1=Mia Ø |last2=Afzal |first2=Shoaib |last3=Vedel-Krogh |first3=Signe |last4=Nielsen |first4=Sune F |last5=Smith |first5=George Davey |last6=Nordestgaard |first6=Børge G |date=2023-08-14 |title=From plasma triglycerides to triglyceride metabolism: effects on mortality in the Copenhagen General Population Study |url=https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/39/4174/7242134 |journal=European Heart Journal |volume=44 |issue=39 |pages=4174–4182 |doi=10.1093/eurheartj/ehad330 |pmid=37575001 |issn=0195-668X|hdl=1983/53cc8321-98e4-4b48-a495-9974a77bb4f9 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref>
